facts.text: An unnamed manufacturer of heavy off-road machines for construction, mining, quarrying and similar work already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.
facts.quote: already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer is developing a system that automatically applies the brakes if the operator does not react.
facts.quote: It is now developing a system that also applies the brakes automatically if the operator does not react.

facts.text: Prototype hardware and software for the heavy off-road automatic braking system will arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software will arrive in mid-2027

facts.text: Validation of the heavy off-road automatic braking system must finish in less than four months after prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software will arrive in mid-2027, and validation must then finish in less than four months.

facts.text: Past validation of a function like the heavy off-road automatic braking system took three to four years, mostly through physical testing and tuning for each machine model.
facts.quote: In the past, validating a function of this kind took three to four years, mostly through physical testing and tuning for each machine model.

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across more than 100 types of job site.
facts.quote: The new system must work across more than 100 types of job site

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across more than 10 operating scenarios per machine.
facts.quote: more than 10 operating scenarios per machine

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work in many weather and light conditions, including rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness and glare.
facts.quote: many weather and light conditions (rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness, glare)

facts.text: The new heavy off-road automatic braking system must work across many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.
facts.quote: many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.

facts.text: Sensor types for the heavy off-road automatic braking system are not confirmed.
facts.quote: The sensor types are not confirmed

facts.text: Because the sensor types are unconfirmed, the validation research had to cover camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other sensor options.
facts.quote: The sensor types are not confirmed, so camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other options all had to be covered.

facts.text: The validation research was required to investigate approaches used in any industry to shorten validation of safety functions that depend on sensors and perception, without assuming one approach was the right one.
facts.quote: Which approaches have been used, in any industry, to shorten the validation of a safety function that depends on sensors and perception?

facts.text: The validation research had to cover simulation of scenes and sensors, replay of recorded field data through software, and software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop and vehicle-in-the-loop testing.
facts.quote: simulation of scenes and sensors; replay of recorded field data through the software; software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop and vehicle-in-the-loop testing

facts.text: The validation research had to cover automated test-track testing with robotic targets, tests with real operators in a machine simulator, and running new software silently on machines already in the field.
facts.quote: automated test-track testing with robotic targets; tests with real operators in a machine simulator; running new software silently on machines already in the field

facts.text: The validation research had to cover staged release with a limited operating range that widens over time, reuse of evidence across similar machine models, and statistical methods; additional approaches were to be added if identified.
facts.quote: staged release with a limited operating range that widens over time; reuse of evidence across similar machine models; and statistical methods. Any approach not on that list was to be added.

facts.text: For each validation approach, the research was to assess what the approach can and cannot prove, required data, models, hardware and people, setup time from zero, cost level, and maturity for heavy off-road machines.
facts.quote: what can it prove and what can it not prove, which inputs does it need (data, models, hardware, people), how long does it take to set up from zero, what is the cost level, and how mature is it for heavy off-road machines?

facts.text: The validation research was to investigate how validation approaches are combined in practice and in what order.
facts.quote: How are these approaches combined in practice, and in what order?

facts.text: The validation research was to investigate which parts of validation cannot be shortened by the proposed approaches, with seasonal weather, durability and formal approvals given as possible examples rather than established findings.
facts.quote: Which parts of validation cannot be shortened by any of these approaches, for example seasonal weather, durability or formal approvals?

facts.text: The validation research was to use documented cases only to assess what a team starting from zero in October 2026 could realistically have working by mid-2027.
facts.quote: Based on documented cases only, what can a team that starts from zero in October 2026 realistically have working by mid-2027?

facts.text: The validation research was required to remain neutral across vendors, products and technologies and cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.
facts.quote: The research was to stay neutral across vendors, products and technologies and to cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.

facts.text: Each important claim in the validation research was to be labeled as an independent study, standard or third-party test; a vendor's own claim; or expert opinion.
facts.quote: Each important claim was to be labeled by its type of evidence (independent study, standard or third-party test; the vendor's own claim; or expert opinion)

facts.text: Every source in the validation research was to be dated, with a preference for software and product sources from 2023 or later.
facts.quote: each source was to be dated, with a preference for sources from 2023 or later for software and products.

facts.text: The validation research was required to report failures, limits and evidence against each approach, not only successes.
facts.quote: Failures, limits and evidence against each approach were to be reported, not only successes.

facts.text: The validation research was required to flag claims proven only for on-road vehicles as on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Anything proven only for on-road vehicles had to be flagged as such

facts.text: Where the validation research could find no evidence, the answer was required to be “not found” rather than a guessed number, price or timeline.
facts.quote: where nothing could be found the answer was to be "not found" rather than a guessed number, price or timeline.
